answers.question: Is AI raised proactively by management, or only in response to analyst questions?
answers.answer: Management proactively raises the topic of AI during their prepared remarks, mentioning Erica, their AI agent, and later discussing productivity improvements from AI. It is also brought up in response to an analyst's question regarding technology spend.

evidence.excerpt: In addition to these stats, I commend you to review Slides 21, 23, and 25. Those highlight the continued progress of digital deployment and activation statistics for each of our businesses. You should note there the impact of Zelle and the continued usage growth and also note the impact of Erica, our AI agent, and its use both across our businesses and with our teammates.
We saw productivity improvements through AI and digitalization more generally, and those enabled us to add client-facing associates as we eliminated work and roles in our operational support areas.

Hi. If you could just give more of an update on technology. What do you expect your spend to be this year versus last year, your spend on AI? And then Slide 21, again, we -- I think everybody appreciates the data you provide on your digital engagement, which is more than others. But no good deed goes unpunished. I'm just looking at Slide 21 and your interactions in consumer with Erica took a dip down in the last year, even while your users go up. So, if you can talk about the spend, investments, and the results from Tech and especially AI.

answers.question: Is AI framed primarily as a revenue/product driver, an efficiency/cost tool, or a competitive necessity?
answers.answer: AI is framed as both a product and an efficiency tool. Management highlights their customer-facing AI agent, Erica, as a key part of their digital deployment. Simultaneously, they emphasize AI's role in driving productivity improvements, enabling headcount to remain flat despite business growth, and reducing roles in operational support.

evidence.excerpt: You should note there the impact of Zelle and the continued usage growth and also note the impact of Erica, our AI agent, and its use both across our businesses and with our teammates.
We saw productivity improvements through AI and digitalization more generally, and those enabled us to add client-facing associates as we eliminated work and roles in our operational support areas.

So, Ken, the number one thing is to continue to let the headcount -- work the headcount through operational excellence and applications of new technologies, including AI that we gave you some sense for. So, as we told you at Investor Day, today's activity in Erica in our consumer business alone is worth thousands of teammates that we don't have to have to do the great work we do for the customers.

answers.question: Does management frame AI's net effect on the business as more opportunity or more risk?
answers.answer: Management frames AI's net effect on the business as an opportunity. Discussions focus on positive outcomes like productivity gains, cost offsets, operational excellence, and improved digital capabilities, with no mention of risks associated with AI.

evidence.excerpt: Beyond that, productivity improvements from AI and digitalization continued to help offset higher wages, benefits, and technology investments.

We apply the digital capabilities, now AI capabilities. And you saw during the year, the headcount was basically flat while we added more people in the field facing off the clients and generating new client flows.

Importantly, we're going through the company to generate more ideas on how to apply AI. And I use example like our audit team has built a capability they think a series of prompts around doing audits and stuff to allow them to shape the headcount back down that they had to grow during the regulatory on side over the last few years. They're going to be able to bring that down and with AI, they'll be able to bring it down further, and they've laid out plans to do that.

answers.question: What tone does management convey when discussing AI (e.g. defensive, cautious, hopeful, excited)?
answers.answer: Management conveys a constructive and optimistic tone when discussing AI. They speak confidently about the productivity gains already achieved, the potential for future headcount reduction through AI, and the generation of new ideas for its application across the company.

evidence.excerpt: So, as we told you at Investor Day, today's activity in Erica in our consumer business alone is worth thousands of teammates that we don't have to have to do the great work we do for the customers.
Next year, we should get more out of it as we figure out and apply it across. So there's different projects going on in the company.

Importantly, we're going through the company to generate more ideas on how to apply AI... So, you're seeing it everywhere in the company. So, there's, I don't know, 15, 20 projects going on, and there will be a laundry list of much bigger size as we go through the company now and are generating ideas now that people are using it and getting used to how to use it.

answers.question: What investment (capex/opex) is disclosed for AI?
answers.answer: Management discloses that the total expenditure on AI is 'several hundred million dollars'.

evidence.excerpt: I don't know off the top of my head the total expenditure, but it's several hundred million dollars.

answers.question: What returns (revenue, cost savings) or costs are attributed to AI, and how is ROI characterized?
answers.answer: The primary return attributed to AI is cost savings through productivity and workforce impact. Management states that activity in their AI agent Erica is 'worth thousands of teammates that we don't have to have'. They also mention using AI to take 30% out of the coding workflow, which 'saves us about 2,000 people'. AI-driven productivity is credited with helping to offset higher wages and investments, and enabling the elimination of roles in operational support.

evidence.excerpt: Beyond that, productivity improvements from AI and digitalization continued to help offset higher wages, benefits, and technology investments.

We saw productivity improvements through AI and digitalization more generally, and those enabled us to add client-facing associates as we eliminated work and roles in our operational support areas.

answers.question: What internal AI use cases are named, and what is their maturity (prototype / production / scaled)?
answers.answer: Several internal AI use cases are mentioned at various stages of maturity. A productivity tool for the company's 18,000 coders is in production, reportedly saving the equivalent of 2,000 people. A 365 CoPilot rollout is scaled across 200,000 teammates. The internal audit team is building a capability using AI prompts to help reduce headcount, which appears to be in a planning or early implementation phase. Management also mentions '15, 20 projects' are ongoing across the company with a larger list of ideas being generated.

for example, under the 365 CoPilot rollout, which is now out across a total of 200,000 teammates using it and learning from it, we expect to get good leverage of that.

answers.question: What customer-facing AI products are named, what is their maturity, and what market/customer feedback is reported?
answers.answer: The only customer-facing AI product named is 'Erica, our AI agent'. It is presented as a scaled, production-level tool used by customers across the businesses. While specific feedback is not detailed, management notes its continued usage growth and points to its contribution to the Consumer Bank's high profit margin. However, an analyst points out that user interactions with Erica dipped in the last year, which the CEO explains is due to the increased use of proactive alerts, reducing the need for customers to ask Erica questions.

evidence.excerpt: you should note there the impact of Zelle and the continued usage growth and also note the impact of Erica, our AI agent, and its use both across our businesses and with our teammates.

The reality of that is -- well, we don't show you the amount of alerts that we deliver. So, you can set up alerts which then has slowed down the need for Erica because the alerts are up to, I think, billions a quarter that are telling you when you're balances are low and things like that, that avoid you having to go in and asking the question.

answers.answer: The company appears to do both. They build proprietary capabilities, as evidenced by the CEO mentioning that their audit team 'has built a capability' using AI prompts. They also leverage external partners, highlighted by the rollout of '365 CoPilot' to 200,000 teammates, which is a Microsoft product.

answers.question: Are new roles, teams, or organizational structures created for AI?
answers.answer: The transcript does not mention the creation of any new roles, teams, or organizational structures specifically for AI. Instead, AI is discussed as a tool being implemented within existing structures, such as the coding and audit teams, to improve efficiency.

answers.question: Is workforce impact (hiring, redeployment, headcount reduction) attributed to AI?
answers.answer: Yes, significant workforce impact is attributed to AI. AI is credited with enabling the elimination of 'work and roles in our operational support areas'. The CEO states that AI techniques applied to coding 'saves us about 2,000 people' and that the activity of their AI agent Erica is 'worth thousands of teammates that we don't have to have'. They also mention the audit team has laid out plans to bring its headcount down with AI. The broader goal is for overall headcount to 'come down during this year' through such applications of new technology.

The rollout of CoPilot to '200,000 teammates' is also specific.
